note: On Their Map, as the brochure sets it out. The eight Marks are the same in every version of the trip: the valley, the impact, the people counted so far, where your share goes and where you sleep do not change. Only the day's title, what you do, who you meet and the swaps change. Edit a day here and every page that shows it changes.

trip.name: On Their Map
trip.line: You came looking for a place that isn't on the map. Leave with your name on theirs.
trip.summary: An 8-day, 7-night community trip with host families in three valleys of Chamba, Himachal Pradesh.
trip.order: The impact comes first, then what you do. Where you sleep comes last.
trip.gettingIn: Chamba town, then 9 km to Chaminoo
trip.seasons: March to May, September to November
trip.note: You stay four nights in Saal Valley and three in Khajjiar; Day 4 is a day trip to Dwat Mahadev. Travel times between the valleys are still being confirmed.

promises.title: People impacted
promises.line: The local people your trip pays directly: hosts, cooks, guides and makers. The count grows on every day page.

promises.title: A cause each day
promises.line: A set share of your trip goes to one named cause each day: a kitchen, a school or a new homestay.

promises.title: Something stays behind
promises.line: An eco-brick in a village bench and a slate on the Feedback Tree. About 90 days later, a note from the village.

marks.impact: Your flour and your dinner keep two things earning: a working gharat, and a family kitchen.
marks.alt: H2O House in the evening: a stone and timber building beside the stream that drives its water mill, with a table set on the flagstones

marks.impact: Saal Valley's homes are new to guests. 4 of 11 are open, with 9 bookings so far. Your stay and your review help the next guest find them.
marks.shareGoesTo: The homestay itself. Your stay is the cause.
marks.tonight: A newly opened homestay, given in rotation (for example Saal River Homestay or Anuradha Kutteer)
marks.alt: A Saal Valley homestay above a stone retaining wall, its upper floor in carved timber, roses in flower by the steps

marks.impact: A craft survives when someone pays for it. You learn from the maker, then you buy from the maker.
marks.alt: A yellow house front in Chamba town with two Gaddi figures painted either side of the doorway

marks.impact: NotOnMap has surveyed 21 panchayats here and spoken to 800+ residents. There are no guests yet. What you say helps decide what gets built first.
marks.tonight: Your Saal Valley homestay (this is a day trip)
marks.fallback: If the valley isn't ready yet: Auda ("Biscuit Point"), with the Ghodawali Mata rock and crafts still in daily use: Kirodu baskets, Charkha spinning, Chakla mats.
marks.alt: A village courtyard house painted blue and green, maize drying in the yard, three residents talking on the step

marks.impact: One more paid service for a kitchen the women own and run. It served 100+ guests in its first three months.
marks.shareGoesTo: SheKitchen, plus the village's own ₹20 Green Fee
marks.tonight: A host family's home in Mystic Village, given in rotation (for example Isro, Brahmi or Babli Devi Kuteer)
marks.alt: Cooking on a wood-fired chullah: dough pressed by hand, roti going onto the pan, a thali eaten on the kitchen floor

marks.impact: Mystic Village wants to become Asia's cleanest village. Each eco-brick ends up in a bench, a wall or a garden.
marks.tonight: A tent on the ridge, Dhaulapir campsite
marks.alt: Tents pitched on the grass at the Dhaulapir campsite, cloud coming over the deodar ridge behind

marks.impact: The women set the terms. They choose what they want to learn from you. In return, they teach you a craft that earns them money.
marks.tonight: A second host family's home, given in rotation
marks.alt: A bonfire outside a village house at dusk, six people sitting round it on low benches

marks.mark: Take a story home, leave yours behind
marks.impact: Folk stories survive when someone listens. Gaon ki Hatti sold out its stock last summer. Its members earned ₹12,000-15,000 each.
marks.shareGoesTo: Gaon ki Hatti, through what you buy
marks.alt: A woman in Gaddi dress, the Luanchadi, on the ridge with the valley behind her

trips.label: Give-back traveller
trips.suits: Couples, friends and solo travellers who want their trip to leave something behind.
trips.changes: The full set of Marks: farm days, the craft makers, the SheKitchen, the eco-brick and the village school.

days.title: Grind maize at a working water mill
do: Arrive via Chamba town, 9 km away.
Walk Chaminoo's fields, past Kathkuni and mud homes.
Grind maize at the gharat, the water-driven stone mill that H2O House is built on.
At dinner, your flour becomes makki ki roti with saag at Meenu Ji's table.
Or try Binda Chacha's special chicken.

days.title: Spend a farm day with a new homestay family
do: Spend the day as part of the household.
Learn the basics of farming maize and wheat.
Harvest vegetables, and milk the cows at Rafi's House.
Afternoon: Chalo Khelo, traditional games with the village children.
Also today: a herbal healing session, or morning yoga by the river.

days.title: Learn Chamba's crafts from their makers
do: In Chamba town, sit with the women who stitch the GI-tagged Chamba rumal.
Meet the makers of the Chamba chappal.
Back at H2O House, paint and carve with valley artists in the open-air studio.
Also today: the 10th-century Lakshmi Narayan temples, and dusk on the Chaugan.
meet: The women who embroider the Chamba rumal
swaps: Folk dance at a district fair

days.title: Walk and listen in Dwat Mahadev
do: A session in the valley's own wellness traditions, including the Yogini traditions now being shaped into experiences.
A listening walk with residents.
Ask what they would like guests to see, and what guests should leave alone.
meet: A local wellness guide, still being chosen

days.title: Cook Gaddi food in a women-run kitchen
do: Walk in under the deodars from Khajjiar via Pukhri, or take the 20-minute 4x4 ride with Manu Kumar or Kaka.
Cook Gaddi food on a wood-fire chullah, with clay pots and vegetables from the family farm.
Learn to make Chamba Chukh.
Eat on the kitchen floor: rajma, makki ki roti, saag.
meet: Shivani, Pooja and Team Udaan, who run the SheKitchen

days.title: Clean up the village and make an eco-brick
do: Start with a morning on the farm (drying maize, in autumn).
Join Team Parivartan's weekly cleanup and fill an eco-brick.
Turn waste into craft with Neelam Sharma, who teaches plastic upcycling at Lambo Devi Kuteer.
Evening: stargazing, then a night in a tent at the Dhaulapir campsite.

days.title: Teach at the village school, learn a craft
do: Morning: visit the area's only school. Share your work and help with a lesson.
Afternoon: swap skills with the women. You teach what they ask for.
They teach you pine-needle craft, weaving or crochet.
Also today: a Gaddi life walk with a villager, and sunrise over Kalatop.

days.title: Hear Gaddi folk tales and buy from local makers
do: Dress in Gaddi clothes (Luanchadi or Chola-Dora).
Listen to folk tales and songs.
Buy what you learned to make.
Paint your slate for the Feedback Tree, then receive your Map of Marks.
On the way out: Khajjiar meadow and lake, then 22 km to Dalhousie.
meet: The makers of Gaon ki Hatti

trips.label: Family
trips.suits: Parents with children. Each experience shows its youngest age.
trips.changes: Shorter walks, games with village children, rolling roti together and a night in a tent.

days.title: Watch a water mill grind your family's flour
do: Arrive via Chamba town, 9 km away.
Take the gharat tour: watch the wooden wheel turn grain into flour (ages 5 and up).
A short walk through Chaminoo's fields, past Kathkuni and mud homes.
Evening: a riverside barbeque by lantern light on the stone deck (March to June, September to November).
Dinner: makki ki roti and saag at Meenu Ji's table.

days.title: Spend a farm day with a new homestay family
do: Spend the day as part of the household.
Help harvest vegetables, and milk the cows at Rafi's House.

Grown-ups can add a herbal healing session (ages 12 and up).

days.title: Paint and carve with the valley's artists

In Chamba town, sit with the women who stitch the GI-tagged Chamba rumal.

days.title: Meet a valley that has no guests yet

days.title: Roll roti in a women-run kitchen
do: Walk in under the deodars from Khajjiar via Pukhri (about 1.5 km), or take the 4x4.

Roll your own makki ki roti.

Fill an eco-brick together. It ends up in a bench, a wall or a garden.
Make something from waste with Neelam Sharma.
Evening: stargazing, then a night in a tent at the Dhaulapir campsite.
swaps: Birdwatching on the ridge (ages 8 and up)

days.title: Swap skills with the women of Mystic Village
do: Grown-ups (16 and up): swap skills with the women. You teach what they ask for.
They teach you pine-needle craft, weaving or crochet.
Children play Chalo Khelo games with the village children.
With children aged 12 and up, visit the village school and help with a lesson.

days.title: Dress in Gaddi clothes and hear the old stories
do: Dress in Gaddi clothes (Luanchadi or Chola-Dora).
Listen to folk tales and songs.
Buy what you learned to make at Gaon ki Hatti.
Paint your family's slate for the Feedback Tree, then receive your Map of Marks.

trips.label: Trekker
trips.suits: Walkers and small groups who want longer days on hill paths.
trips.changes: Walks along the rivers, an adventure day, the longer Rota walk in, a morning with the herders and the Pohlani Mata trek.

days.title: Walk the Saal to a working water mill
do: Arrive via Chamba town, 9 km away.
Walk along the Saal and the Hul Nala, which meet below H2O House.
Grind maize at the gharat that H2O House is built on.
At dinner, your flour becomes makki ki roti with saag at Meenu Ji's table.

days.title: Farm in the morning, rappel in the afternoon
do: Morning: farm maize and wheat with your homestay family.
Milk the cows at Rafi's House.
Afternoon: adventure day at Nomadic Hikes, with rappelling, zip-lining and more (ages 12 and up; March to June, September to November).

days.title: Learn Chamba's crafts, then walk the old town
do: In Chamba town, sit with the women who stitch the GI-tagged Chamba rumal.
Meet the makers of the Chamba chappal.
Walk the old town to the 10th-century Lakshmi Narayan temples.
meet: The women who embroider the Chamba rumal

days.title: Walk Dwat Mahadev's paths with the people who live there
do: A longer listening walk on valley paths with residents.
Ask what they would like guests to see, and what guests should leave alone.

days.title: Walk in to Mystic Village and cook on the chullah

They teach you pine-needle craft, weaving or crochet.

days.title: Hear the old stories, then walk out to Khajjiar

Buy what you learned to make at Gaon ki Hatti.

Walk out to Khajjiar meadow and lake.

trips.changes: Yoga by the river, herbal healing, Dwat Mahadev's wellness traditions, birdwatching and a day off the grid.

Watch the gharat's wooden wheel grind maize into flour.
Dinner: your flour as makki ki roti with saag at Meenu Ji's table.

days.title: Learn the valley's healing plants
do: A herbal healing session: the hill plants of the valley and how they are used.
A slow morning on the farm with your homestay family.
Afternoon: rest, or join the Chalo Khelo games with the village children.

A day off the grid: almost no phone signal, and time in the meadow.
Afternoon: swap skills with the women. They teach you pine-needle craft, weaving or crochet.

trips.suits: Schools and colleges. Groups are split across host homes, so ask us first.
trips.changes: Rural life, crafts, history and ecology: the water mill, a waste count, and a lesson exchange at the village school.

days.title: Learn how a water mill grinds grain

Gharat tour: how a water-driven stone mill turns grain into village flour.
A village walk through Chaminoo's fields, past Kathkuni and mud homes.
Dinner in small groups with host families.

do: Learn the basics of farming maize and wheat.
Harvest vegetables, and milk the cows at Rafi's House.

days.title: Study Chamba's crafts and history
do: Sit with the women who stitch the GI-tagged Chamba rumal.

Visit the Bhuri Singh Museum.
Walk to the 10th-century Lakshmi Narayan temples.
meet: The women who embroider the Chamba rumal

days.title: Listen to a valley before it opens to guests

trust.line: NotOnMap has reached 800+ people. Its Impact Assessment for Mystic Village (April to December 2025) found 87% of visitors satisfied and 3x repeat visits. NotOnMap holds an IRTA Silver award.
trust.source: NotOnMap Impact Assessment, Mystic Village, April to December 2025

consent: People are named only with their consent. Figures come from NotOnMap's reports for 2025-26. The share of your trip that goes to each cause will be fixed before you book.
